history.dynasty: None (gurdwara is a modern shrine; the fort it stands in traces its origins to the Kushana period - emperor Kanishka per tradition - and 1100-1200 AD)
history.period: Gurdwara: modern construction (date unverified); Fort: ancient, recognised as a monument of national importance maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a SIKH gurdwara, not a Hindu temple. Gurdwara Qila Mubarak Sahib stands inside the ancient Qila Mubarak fort in the heart of Bathinda city (the oldest surviving fort in India in its current form, dating to 1100-1200 AD, whose bricks date to the Kushana period when Kanishka ruled; Razia Sultan, the first woman to rule the Delhi throne, was imprisoned here in 1240). Travel accounts note that the fort houses TWO historic gurdwaras inside its mud-brick walls, and that the fort complex has no closing timings because of the religious places inside. Sikh tradition associates Bathinda with Guru Nanak (first udasi encounter with the faqir Haji Rattan near the fort), Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji (who visited Bathinda), and Guru Gobind Singh Ji (who came to Bathinda via Bhuchon and Bhago and halted at the Haji Rattan mausoleum). IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: this is NOT the Qila Mubarak palace complex at Patiala (the Patiala royal complex of Maharaja Ala Singh, ~130 km away) - this gurdwara is inside the Bathinda fort. Some travel write-ups conflate the two; the location is verified as Bathinda by multiple visitor reviews.

name: Qila Mubarak Gurudwara
town: Bathinda (CSV town correct - the fort and gurdwara are in the heart of Bathinda city)
town_description: Bathinda is an ancient city of the Malwa region of Punjab (population ~2.85 lakh, 2011), once the seat of Raja Dab, briefly occupied by Muhammad Ghori (1189) and retaken by Prithvi Raj Chauhan (1191), conquered by Maharaja Ala Singh of Patiala circa 1754, and later a full-fledged district of PEPSU and Punjab. Its landmarks are the Qila Mubarak fort (ASI-protected), the Haji Rattan dargah-gurdwara-mosque complex, and Bathinda Lake.

travel.airport: Bathinda Airport (BUP) has limited commercial service; Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~190 km) is the nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Bathinda Junction - one of North India's largest rail junctions; the fort is in the old city, a short auto-rickshaw ride away.
travel.road: Qila Mubarak fort is in the heart of Bathinda city; the gurdwara is inside the fort complex, reachable on foot through the fort gates.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (Punjab plains are extremely hot April-June).
visitor_information.opening_hours: The fort complex has no closing timings due to the religious places inside (per travel accounts - verify on arrival).
